evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1e and o.

claim: Pax2Cre activity was not detected in dorsal root ganglia.
source: Pax2Cre activity was not detected in several known postotic cranial/cardiac and trunk neural crest derivatives including dorsal root ganglia and sympathetic ganglia (Figure 1—figure supplement 1m and n) and mesenchyme of the cardiac outflow tract (Figure 1—figure supplement 2c).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1m and n.

claim: Pax2Cre activity was not detected in sympathetic ganglia.
source: Pax2Cre activity was not detected in several known postotic cranial/cardiac and trunk neural crest derivatives including dorsal root ganglia and sympathetic ganglia (Figure 1—figure supplement 1m and n) and mesenchyme of the cardiac outflow tract (Figure 1—figure supplement 2c).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1m and n.

claim: Pax2Cre activity was not detected in mesenchyme of the cardiac outflow tract.
source: Pax2Cre activity was not detected in several known postotic cranial/cardiac and trunk neural crest derivatives including dorsal root ganglia and sympathetic ganglia (Figure 1—figure supplement 1m and n) and mesenchyme of the cardiac outflow tract (Figure 1—figure supplement 2c).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2c.

claim: Prominent endogenous Pax2 was detected in the lens and otic vesicle at E9.5-10.0.
source: Prominent endogenous Pax2 was detected in the lens and otic vesicle (both known placode derivatives), in intermediate mesoderm (future kidneys), and germane to this report also in the postotic pharyngeal arches that abut vagal neural crest (Figure 1—figure supplement 2a and b).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2a and b.

claim: Endogenous Pax2 was detected in intermediate mesoderm at E9.5-10.0.
source: Prominent endogenous Pax2 was detected in the lens and otic vesicle (both known placode derivatives), in intermediate mesoderm (future kidneys), and germane to this report also in the postotic pharyngeal arches that abut vagal neural crest (Figure 1—figure supplement 2a and b).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2a and b.

claim: Endogenous Pax2 was detected in the postotic pharyngeal arches that abut vagal neural crest at E9.5-10.0.
source: Prominent endogenous Pax2 was detected in the lens and otic vesicle (both known placode derivatives), in intermediate mesoderm (future kidneys), and germane to this report also in the postotic pharyngeal arches that abut vagal neural crest (Figure 1—figure supplement 2a and b).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2a and b.

claim: Pax2 protein overlapped Pax2Cre-labeled pharyngeal ectoderm and Pax2Cre-labeled mesenchymal cells just at the stage of delamination from the ectoderm.
source: Pax2 protein overlapped Pax2Cre-labeled pharyngeal ectoderm and Pax2Cre-labeled mesenchymal cells just at the stage of delamination from the ectoderm, although Pax2 expression was downregulated with migration and therefore not detected in most Pax2Cre lineage-labeled mesenchymal cells in the postotic domain (Figure 1—figure supplement 2c and d).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2c and d.

claim: Pax2 expression was downregulated with migration and therefore not detected in most Pax2Cre lineage-labeled mesenchymal cells in the postotic domain.
source: Pax2 protein overlapped Pax2Cre-labeled pharyngeal ectoderm and Pax2Cre-labeled mesenchymal cells just at the stage of delamination from the ectoderm, although Pax2 expression was downregulated with migration and therefore not detected in most Pax2Cre lineage-labeled mesenchymal cells in the postotic domain (Figure 1—figure supplement 2c and d).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2c and d.

claim: Pax2 expression was excluded from the territory of pharyngeal neural crest marked by the Wnt1Cre lineage label.
source: In contrast, Pax2 expression was excluded from the territory of pharyngeal neural crest marked by the Wnt1Cre lineage label (Figure 1—figure supplement 2e and f).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 2e and f.

claim: The entirety of Wnt1Cre-labeled cells expressed AP2 at E9.75.
source: We observed that the entirety of Wnt1Cre-labeled cells expressed AP2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 3e and f).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 3e and f.

claim: Sox10 expression was associated with a subset of the Wnt1Cre-labeled cell population at E9.75.
source: Sox10 expression was associated with a subset of the Wnt1Cre-labeled cell population, and thus with a subset of AP2-expressing arch mesenchymal cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 3e and f).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 3e and f.

claim: Neither AP2 nor Sox10 were expressed in any migratory Pax2Cre lineage-labeled cells at E9.75.
source: In contrast, although there was overlap of AP2 expression with Pax2Cre in the ectoderm, neither AP2 nor Sox10 were expressed in any migratory Pax2Cre lineage-labeled cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 3g and h).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 3g and h.

claim: Only 11.8±1.2% of the counted cells in E10.5 Pax2Cre/Rosa26nT-nG embryos were Pax2Cre-derived.
source: In Pax2Cre/Rosa26nT-nG embryos (six embryos from different litters, average 249.7±15.7 counted cells per embryo), only 11.8±1.2% of the counted cells were Pax2Cre-derived (Figure 2v, black and gray bars); the other 88% (Figure 2v, white bar) are presumed to be Wnt1Cre-derived Ret+ cells (which was directly measured at 86% as described below).
evidence: This is stated as a quantitative observation with reference to Figure 2v.

claim: Ret was expressed in 14.4±1.7% of the Pax2Cre lineage-labeled cells at E10.5.
source: Ret was expressed in 14.4±1.7% of the Pax2Cre lineage-labeled cells, but only 1.6±0.2% of the total counted cells.
evidence: This is stated as a quantitative observation.

claim: Almost all (97.8±0.2%) counted cells in E10.5 Wnt1Cre/Rosa26nT-nG embryos were lineage labeled.
source: We performed the same analysis for the Wnt1Cre lineage (six embryos; 178.8±11.4 counted cells per embryo). Here, almost all (97.8±0.2%) counted cells were lineage labeled, and of these, 86.2±1.5% expressed Ret.
evidence: This is stated as a quantitative observation.

claim: 86.2±1.5% of Wnt1Cre-labeled cells expressed Ret at E10.5.
source: We performed the same analysis for the Wnt1Cre lineage (six embryos; 178.8±11.4 counted cells per embryo). Here, almost all (97.8±0.2%) counted cells were lineage labeled, and of these, 86.2±1.5% expressed Ret.
evidence: This is stated as a quantitative observation.

claim: 97.5% of the Ret-expressing cells in E10.5 Wnt1Cre/Rosa26nT-nG embryos were of the Wnt1Cre lineage.
source: Consequently, 97.5% of the Ret-expressing cells in Wnt1Cre/Rosa26nT-nG embryos were of this lineage.
evidence: This is stated as a calculated result from the quantitative observations.

claim: Ret-expressing cells in the E10.5 midgut are overwhelmingly derived from the Wnt1Cre lineage.
source: These results indicate that Ret-expressing cells in the E10.5 midgut are overwhelmingly derived from the Wnt1Cre lineage.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the quantitative observations.

claim: The majority of Wnt1Cre-derived cells at E10.5 in the midgut express Ret whereas only a minor population of Pax2Cre-derived cells does so.
source: The majority of Wnt1Cre-derived cells at E10.5 in the midgut express Ret whereas only a minor population of Pax2Cre-derived cells does so.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the quantitative observations.

claim: Pax2Cre and Wnt1Cre delineate molecularly distinct populations of early migratory ENS progenitor cells.
source: This further supports the idea that Pax2Cre and Wnt1Cre delineate molecularly distinct populations of early migratory ENS progenitor cells.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the observations.

claim: Approximately half of colonic myenteric ganglion cells were labeled with either Pax2Cre or Wnt1Cre lineage marker at P9.
source: First, based on morphology and expression of the pan-neuronal marker Hu, approximately half of colonic myenteric ganglion cells were labeled with either lineage marker (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a, b, g, pie chart).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1a, b, g.

claim: All or most ENS neurons are derived from either a Pax2Cre or a Wnt1Cre lineage.
source: Because the sum of the two individual estimates is close to 100%, this is consistent with the proposition that all or most ENS neurons are derived from either a Pax2Cre or a Wnt1Cre lineage and that the two Cre lines are mostly if not fully nonoverlapping in their recombination domains.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the quantitative observations.

claim: Mechanosensory neurons release the excitatory neurotransmitter calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) to initiate peristaltic contractions in guinea pig colon.
source: Electrophysiology studies of guinea pig colon showed that mechanosensory neurons release the excitatory neurotransmitter calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) to initiate peristaltic contractions (Sarna, 2010).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Sarna, 2010.

claim: CGRP+ neurons in the postnatal P9 mouse distal colon are located in the myenteric plexus and send their projections to the gut luminal epithelium, consistent with a mechanosensory fate.
source: By immunostaining, we identified that CGRP+ neurons in the postnatal P9 mouse distal colon are located in the myenteric plexus and send their projections to the gut luminal epithelium, consistent with a mechanosensory fate (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3b.

claim: Nitric oxide synthase (NOS) is recognized as a marker for both inhibitory interneurons and inhibitory motor neurons.
source: Nitric oxide synthase (NOS) is recognized as a marker for both inhibitory interneurons and inhibitory motor neurons (Costa et al., 1992; Timmermans et al., 1994; Sang and Young, 1996).
evidence: This is stated with citations to Costa et al., 1992; Timmermans et al., 1994; Sang and Young, 1996.

claim: In the mouse P9 colon, NOS+ neurons are found in the myenteric ganglia and their axons are found exclusively within the circular muscle layer.
source: In the mouse P9 colon, NOS+ neurons are found in the myenteric ganglia and their axons are found exclusively within the circular muscle layer (Figure 3c), implying that these represent at least a subset of motor neurons.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3c.

claim: NOS+ neurons in the mouse P9 colon represent at least a subset of motor neurons.
source: In the mouse P9 colon, NOS+ neurons are found in the myenteric ganglia and their axons are found exclusively within the circular muscle layer (Figure 3c), implying that these represent at least a subset of motor neurons.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the observation with reference to Figure 3c.

claim: Only approximately one-third of neurons of both Pax2Cre and Wnt1Cre lineages in the distal colon were CGRP+ or NOS+ at P9.
source: Only approximately one-third of neurons of both lineages in the distal colon were CGRP+ or NOS+ (Figure 3—figure supplement 1g, bar graph), which means that additional neuronal fates (white bars in Figure 3—figure supplement 1g) are taken by both lineages (which is expected).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1g.

claim: Less than 10% of myenteric ganglion neurons were CGRP+ at P9.
source: Less than 10% of myenteric ganglion neurons were CGRP+ (Figure 3—figure supplement 1h, pie chart).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1h.

claim: The vast majority (>90%) of CGRP+ myenteric ganglion neurons were Pax2Cre-derived at P9.
source: Strikingly, the vast majority (>90%) of these were Pax2Cre-derived (Figure 3d, Figure 3—figure supplement 1c, d, h, bar graph).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3d, Figure 3—figure supplement 1c, d, h.

claim: A minimum number (approx. 3%) of CGRP+ neurons were labeled by Wnt1Cre at P9.
source: A minimum number (approx. 3%) of CGRP+ neurons were labeled by Wnt1Cre (Figure 3f, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, 1h, bar graph), which indicates that Wnt1Cre-derived cells have little or no commitment to a mechanosensory fate in the distal colon.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3f, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, 1h.

claim: Wnt1Cre-derived cells have little or no commitment to a mechanosensory fate in the distal colon.
source: A minimum number (approx. 3%) of CGRP+ neurons were labeled by Wnt1Cre (Figure 3f, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, 1h, bar graph), which indicates that Wnt1Cre-derived cells have little or no commitment to a mechanosensory fate in the distal colon.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the observation with reference to Figure 3f, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, 1h.

claim: Approx. 25% of myenteric ganglion neurons were NOS+ at P9.
source: Approx. 25% of myenteric ganglion neurons were NOS+.
evidence: This is stated as an observation.

claim: The majority of NOS+ myenteric ganglion neurons were derived from the Wnt1Cre lineage at P9.
source: The majority of these were derived from the Wnt1Cre lineage (Figure 3g, Figure 3—figure supplement 1f, h, bar graph), although Pax2Cre-derived neurons also gave rise to a NOS-reactive population of the distal colon (Figure 3e, Figure 3—figure supplement 1e, h, bar graph).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3g, Figure 3—figure supplement 1f, h.

claim: Pax2Cre-derived neurons also gave rise to a NOS-reactive population of the distal colon at P9.
source: The majority of these were derived from the Wnt1Cre lineage (Figure 3g, Figure 3—figure supplement 1f, h, bar graph), although Pax2Cre-derived neurons also gave rise to a NOS-reactive population of the distal colon (Figure 3e, Figure 3—figure supplement 1e, h, bar graph).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3e, Figure 3—figure supplement 1e, h.

claim: Pax2Cre/Ednrb mutant guts exhibited a profound reduction of CGRP+ axons projecting toward the colonic lumen in the transition zone at P9.
source: In this transition zone, we observed a profound reduction of CGRP+ axons projecting toward the colonic lumen in Pax2Cre/Ednrb mutant guts (Figure 3j and p), equal to that in global Ednrb mutants (Figure 3i and p), whereas NOS+ axons in the circular muscle were present normally in the adjacent section (Figure 3n and q).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3j and p.

claim: NOS+ axons in the circular muscle were present normally in Pax2Cre/Ednrb mutant guts in the transition zone at P9.
source: In this transition zone, we observed a profound reduction of CGRP+ axons projecting toward the colonic lumen in Pax2Cre/Ednrb mutant guts (Figure 3j and p), equal to that in global Ednrb mutants (Figure 3i and p), whereas NOS+ axons in the circular muscle were present normally in the adjacent section (Figure 3n and q).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3n and q.

claim: Wnt1Cre/Ednrb mutant guts exhibited abundant CGRP+ axons projecting toward sensory epithelium in the transition zone at P9.
source: Wnt1Cre/Ednrb mutant guts exhibited abundant CGRP+ axons projecting toward sensory epithelium (Figure 3k and p) while their circular muscle layers showed a total loss of NOS+ axonal innervation (Figure 3o and q).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3k and p.

claim: Wnt1Cre/Ednrb mutant guts showed a total loss of NOS+ axonal innervation in the circular muscle layers in the transition zone at P9.
source: Wnt1Cre/Ednrb mutant guts exhibited abundant CGRP+ axons projecting toward sensory epithelium (Figure 3k and p) while their circular muscle layers showed a total loss of NOS+ axonal innervation (Figure 3o and q).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 3o and q.

claim: In the transition area, defective migration of Pax2Cre-derived enteric progenitor cells results in selective loss of myenteric mechanosensory neurons, while myenteric motor neurons and their innervations of the circular muscle were not affected.
source: Thus, in the transition area, defective migration of Pax2Cre-derived enteric progenitor cells results in selective loss of myenteric mechanosensory neurons, while myenteric motor neurons and their innervations of the circular muscle were not affected.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the observations.

claim: Defective migration of Wnt1Cre-derived ENS progenitors results in selective loss of motor neurons with no impact on the mechanosensory neuron population.
source: Reciprocally, defective migration of Wnt1Cre-derived ENS progenitors results in selective loss of motor neurons with no impact on the mechanosensory neuron population.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the observations.

claim: Pax2Cre-labeled and Wnt1Cre-labeled cells have a distinct and nonoverlapping marker expression program during their embryonic migration.
source: These results collectively demonstrate that Pax2Cre-labeled and Wnt1Cre-labeled cells have a distinct and nonoverlapping marker expression program during their embryonic migration, and have a distinct set of terminal differentiation fates in the postnatal distal colon.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the observations.

claim: Pax2Cre-labeled and Wnt1Cre-labeled cells have a distinct set of terminal differentiation fates in the postnatal distal colon.
source: These results collectively demonstrate that Pax2Cre-labeled and Wnt1Cre-labeled cells have a distinct and nonoverlapping marker expression program during their embryonic migration, and have a distinct set of terminal differentiation fates in the postnatal distal colon.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the observations.

claim: Neither Pax2Cre nor Wnt1Cre lineage can modulate its normal fate to compensate for the absence of the other.
source: A further conclusion from the analysis of conditional Ednrb mutants is that neither lineage can modulate its normal fate to compensate for the absence of the other.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the observations.

claim: A previous study documented Hirschsprung disease phenotypes in mice with conditional Ret mutation in the Wnt1Cre domain (Wnt1Cre/Ret mutants), including lethality around postnatal day 21.
source: A previous study (Luo et al., 2007) documented Hirschsprung disease phenotypes in mice with conditional Ret mutation in the Wnt1Cre domain (Wnt1Cre/Ret mutants), including lethality around postnatal day 21.
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Luo et al., 2007.

claim: Global Ret deficiency results in neonatal lethality because of renal agenesis.
source: Global Ret deficiency results in neonatal lethality because of renal agenesis (Schuchardt et al., 1994; Durbec et al., 1996), and because Pax2Cre is expressed in intermediate mesoderm, Pax2Cre/Ret mutants in our colony also died in the early postnatal period.
evidence: This is stated with citations to Schuchardt et al., 1994; Durbec et al., 1996.

claim: Pax2Cre/Ret mutants died in the early postnatal period because Pax2Cre is expressed in intermediate mesoderm.
source: Global Ret deficiency results in neonatal lethality because of renal agenesis (Schuchardt et al., 1994; Durbec et al., 1996), and because Pax2Cre is expressed in intermediate mesoderm, Pax2Cre/Ret mutants in our colony also died in the early postnatal period.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and inference.

claim: In Pax2Cre/Ret/Rosa26lacZ mutant embryos at E12.5, there was an obvious deficiency of Pax2Cre-labeled cells migrating throughout the midgut, and no Pax2Cre-labeled cells migrated caudally beyond the cecum.
source: In Pax2Cre/Ret/Rosa26lacZ mutant embryos at E12.5, we observed an obvious deficiency of Pax2Cre-labeled cells migrating throughout the midgut, and no Pax2Cre-labeled cells migrated caudally beyond the cecum (Figure 4b), whereas lineage-labeled cells reached the terminal hindgut in littermate controls (Figure 4a).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 4b.

claim: Ret function is required within the Pax2Cre lineage for ENS progenitor migration.
source: This result implies a function for Ret within the Pax2Cre lineage.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the observation.

claim: A substantially larger fraction of Pax2Cre-labeled cells in the distal midgut in control E11.5 Pax2Cre/Rosa26nT-nG embryos expressed Ret relative to E10.5.
source: We found that a substantially larger fraction of Pax2Cre-labeled cells in the distal midgut (at the migratory wavefront) in control E11.5 Pax2Cre/Rosa26nT-nG embryos expressed Ret (Figure 2m and y, black bar) relative to E10.5 (Figure 2w, black bar).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 2m and y, Figure 2w.

claim: The Pax2Cre-labeled population in control embryos expands significantly during the E10.5–11.5 period.
source: This demonstrates that the Pax2Cre-labeled population in control embryos expands significantly during the E10.5–11.5 period.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the observation.

claim: At E10.5, p75-expressing enteric progenitors included Pax2Cre lineage cells co-migrating with non-Pax2Cre cells.
source: At E10.5, p75-expressing enteric progenitors included Pax2Cre lineage cells co-migrating with non-Pax2Cre cells (Figure 4i), the latter which presumably consists of Wnt1Cre-derived cells.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 4i.

claim: In Pax2Cre/Ret mutant embryos at E10.5, p75-expressing cells again included those with and without the Pax2Cre lineage label, demonstrating a normal caudal progression.
source: In Pax2Cre/Ret mutant embryos at this stage, p75-expressing cells again included those with and without the Pax2Cre lineage label, demonstrating a normal caudal progression (Figure 4j).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 4j.

claim: Overall ENS progenitor cell number was already affected as early as E10.5 in the Pax2Cre/Ret mutant background.
source: Quantitative evaluation, however, indicated that overall ENS progenitor cell number was already affected as early as E10.5 in the Pax2Cre/Ret mutant background (Figure 2w): both the Pax2Cre-derived cell population and the Ret-expressing non-Pax2Cre population were reduced by half, and therefore the total number of countable cells (expressing one or both markers) per midgut from each mutant embryo was also reduced by half.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 2w.

claim: Ret deficiency in the Pax2Cre lineage impacts ENS progenitor cells derived from the Pax2Cre lineage as well as from the presumptive Wnt1Cre lineage, starting as the migratory cells enter the midgut.
source: The interpretation of this analysis is that Ret deficiency in the Pax2Cre lineage impacts ENS progenitor cells derived from the Pax2Cre lineage as well as from the presumptive Wnt1Cre lineage, starting as the migratory cells enter the midgut.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the observations.

claim: Wnt1Cre-labeled cells at E12.5 populated the esophagus and stomach but failed to migrate into the intestine in Wnt1Cre/Ret mutants.
source: Wnt1Cre-labeled cells at E12.5 populated the esophagus and stomach but failed to migrate into the intestine (Figure 4d), which recapitulates the global Ret mutant phenotype (Schuchardt et al., 1994; Durbec et al., 1996).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 4d and citations to Schuchardt et al., 1994; Durbec et al., 1996.

claim: Wnt1Cre/Ret mutants exhibited total loss of enteric progenitor cells along the entire axis of the developing intestine at E12.5.
source: Wholemount 2H3 staining confirmed the total loss of enteric progenitor cells along the entire axis of the developing intestine (Figure 4h).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 4h.

claim: Ret function in the Wnt1Cre domain is absolutely required for migration of all enteric progenitors, Wnt1Cre-derived as well as non-Wnt1Cre-derived (i.e. Pax2Cre-derived), into and through the intestinal tract.
source: These results demonstrate that Ret function in the Wnt1Cre domain is absolutely required for migration of all enteric progenitors, Wnt1Cre-derived as well as non-Wnt1Cre-derived (i.e. Pax2Cre-derived), into and through the intestinal tract.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the observations.

claim: GDNF induced robust radial outgrowth from control midgut slices, which included a mixed population of neurons and glia; Pax2Cre lineage cells were present in these outgrowths.
source: GDNF induced robust radial outgrowth from control midgut slices, which included a mixed population of neurons and glia; Pax2Cre lineage cells were present in these outgrowths (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 5b.

claim: Pax2Cre/Ret mutant gut explants exhibited little or no outgrowth in response to GDNF.
source: Pax2Cre/Ret mutant gut explants, however, exhibited little or no outgrowth in response to GDNF (Figure 5c and g), even though lineage-positive, Hu-positive, and BLBP-positive cells are present in the explant itself.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 5c and g.

claim: There were no lineage negative outgrowths in response to GDNF in Pax2Cre/Ret explants.
source: Importantly, Ret-expressing non-Pax2Cre lineage (i.e. likely Wnt1Cre-derived) cells are present throughout the midgut at E10.5 (Figure 2f and w), yet there were no lineage negative outgrowths in response to GDNF in Pax2Cre/Ret explants (Figure 5c).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 5c.

claim: The Wnt1Cre-derived cells in the midgut do not harbor a cell-autonomous migratory response to GDNF, but instead require co-migration with Pax2Cre lineage cells.
source: This indicates that the Wnt1Cre-derived cells in the midgut do not harbor a cell-autonomous migratory response to GDNF, but instead require co-migration with Pax2Cre lineage cells.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the observations.

claim: ENS progenitor migration is an orchestrated process that requires GDNF response in both Pax2Cre and Wnt1Cre progenitor populations.
source: Collectively, we interpret these results to show that ENS progenitor migration is an orchestrated process that requires GDNF response in both Pax2Cre and Wnt1Cre progenitor populations.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the results.

claim: Each ENS progenitor lineage requires migratory function (i.e. Ret function) in the other, albeit at different times and locations along the gut axis.
source: To support migration, each progenitor lineage requires migratory function (i.e. Ret function) in the other, albeit at different times and locations along the gut axis: Ret deficiency in the Wnt1Cre lineage blocks migration of both lineages at the duodenum, whereas Ret deficiency in the Pax2Cre lineage blocks migration of both lineages at the hindgut.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the results.

claim: Ret deficiency in the Wnt1Cre lineage blocks migration of both lineages at the duodenum.
source: To support migration, each progenitor lineage requires migratory function (i.e. Ret function) in the other, albeit at different times and locations along the gut axis: Ret deficiency in the Wnt1Cre lineage blocks migration of both lineages at the duodenum, whereas Ret deficiency in the Pax2Cre lineage blocks migration of both lineages at the hindgut.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the results.

claim: Ret deficiency in the Pax2Cre lineage blocks migration of both lineages at the hindgut.
source: To support migration, each progenitor lineage requires migratory function (i.e. Ret function) in the other, albeit at different times and locations along the gut axis: Ret deficiency in the Wnt1Cre lineage blocks migration of both lineages at the duodenum, whereas Ret deficiency in the Pax2Cre lineage blocks migration of both lineages at the hindgut.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the results.

claim: Neither EDN3 nor NGF promoted enteric progenitor cell outgrowth compared to the activity of GDNF in E10.5 explants.
source: While explanted gut sections at E10.5 contain cells that express p75 and Hu, neither EDN3 nor NGF promoted enteric progenitor cell outgrowth compared to the activity of GDNF (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: At E11.5, EDN3 and NGF induced only minimal outgrowth from both Pax2Cre- and Wnt1Cre lineage-labeled midgut sections.
source: Similarly, at E11.5, EDN3 and NGF induced only minimal outgrowth from both Pax2Cre- and Wnt1Cre lineage-labeled midgut sections (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Edn3-Ednrb signaling does not by itself induce migration of either Pax2Cre-labeled or Wnt1Cre-labeled enteric progenitors.
source: Impaired cell migration in vivo (Figure 1f and h) has at various times been previously interpreted in global Edn3 and Ednrb mutants to represent a chemoattractive role for Edn3-Ednrb signaling, but as previously shown in vitro (Barlow et al., 2003; Goto et al., 2013; Nagy and Goldstein, 2017) and in our results, Edn3-Ednrb signaling does not by itself induce migration of either Pax2Cre-labeled or Wnt1Cre-labeled enteric progenitors.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the observations and prior studies with citations to Barlow et al., 2003; Goto et al., 2013; Nagy and Goldstein, 2017.

claim: GDNF-Ret signaling is the major mechanism that supports ENS progenitor migration.
source: The in vitro explant assays clearly demonstrate that GDNF-Ret signaling is the major mechanism that supports ENS progenitor migration.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the in vitro explant assays.

claim: Pax2Cre/Ednrb mutant explants showed a blunted response to GDNF compared to control cells across the rostral-caudal axis of the E11.5 midgut.
source: Across the rostral-caudal axis of the midgut, Pax2Cre/Ednrb mutant explants showed a blunted response to GDNF compared to control cells (Figure 6a and c), which was more severe at the distal end (Figure 6b, d, i, and j), even though lineage-positive cells were present.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 6a and c.

claim: Wnt1Cre/Ednrb mutant midgut segments exhibited a similar trend as Pax2Cre/Ednrb mutant midgut in both proximal and distal segments, including greater impairment of GDNF responsiveness at the migratory wavefront.
source: Wnt1Cre/Ednrb mutant midgut segments exhibited a similar trend as Pax2Cre/Ednrb mutant midgut in both proximal (Figure 6e, g, and k) and distal segments (Figure 6f, h, and l), including greater impairment of GDNF responsiveness at the migratory wavefront.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 6e, g, k, f, h, and l.

claim: The Pax2Cre and Wnt1Cre lineages both rely on endothelin signaling to fully populate the gut with GDNF-responsive cells.
source: These results show that the Pax2Cre and Wnt1Cre lineages both rely on endothelin signaling to fully populate the gut with GDNF-responsive cells, and imply that endothelin signaling is needed to support GDNF responsiveness in enteric progenitors.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the observations.

claim: Endothelin signaling is needed to support GDNF responsiveness in enteric progenitors.
source: These results show that the Pax2Cre and Wnt1Cre lineages both rely on endothelin signaling to fully populate the gut with GDNF-responsive cells, and imply that endothelin signaling is needed to support GDNF responsiveness in enteric progenitors.
evidence: This is stated as an implication from the observations.

claim: In normal E11.5 embryos, a large fraction of Pax2Cre-derived cells express Ret at the migratory wavefront.
source: As also noted earlier (Figure 2m and y), in normal E11.5 embryos a large fraction of Pax2Cre-derived cells express Ret at the migratory wavefront (Figure 7a and e).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 7a and e.

claim: In the Pax2Cre/Ednrb mutant, Pax2Cre-labeled cells populating the apex of the midgut loop were Ret-negative at E11.5.
source: In the Pax2Cre/Ednrb mutant, however, Pax2Cre-labeled cells populating the apex of the midgut loop were Ret-negative, and the surrounding Ret-expressing cells were mostly unlabeled by the Pax2Cre lineage marker (Figure 7b and f).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 7b and f.

claim: Absence of Ednrb resulted in far fewer Pax2Cre lineage-derived cells expressing Ret in the more caudal segments at E11.5.
source: The analysis confirmed that absence of Ednrb resulted in far fewer Pax2Cre lineage-derived cells expressing Ret in the more caudal segments (Figure 7i).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 7i.

claim: The expansion of the Ret+ subpopulation of the Pax2Cre lineage that occurs between E10.5 and 11.5 requires Ednrb signaling in a cell-autonomous manner.
source: Thus, the expansion of the Ret+ subpopulation of the Pax2Cre lineage that occurs between E10.5 and 11.5 (Figure 2m and y) requires Ednrb signaling in a cell-autonomous manner.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the observations with reference to Figure 2m and y.

claim: Edn3-Ednrb signaling does not affect Ret expression in Wnt1Cre-derived migratory enteric progenitor cells at E11.5.
source: We performed the same analysis for E11.5 Wnt1Cre/Ednrb/Rosa26nT-nG mutants and their littermate embryos (Figure 7c, d, g, h, and j). Unlike the observation in the Pax2Cre lineage, Edn3-Ednrb signaling does not affect Ret expression in Wnt1Cre-derived migratory enteric progenitor cells.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 7c, d, g, h, and j.

claim: Ednrb-deficient Wnt1Cre-derived cells are unable to respond to GDNF in vivo and in vitro.
source: Nonetheless, these cells are unable to respond to GDNF in vivo (Figure 1h) and in vitro (Figure 6g and h).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 1h, Figure 6g and h.

claim: Phospho-Y1015 signal was only evident in 33% of Ednrb-deficient Wnt1Cre-derived cells at E11.5.
source: An antibody specific for phospho-Ret Y1015 was detected in the majority (87%) of control Wnt1Cre-labeled cells (Figure 7q), also in the cytoplasm and nucleus (Figure 7k, magenta). However, phospho-Y1015 signal was only evident in 33% of Ednrb-deficient Wnt1Cre-derived cells (Figure 7l and q).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 7l and q.

claim: A substantial subpopulation of the Wnt1Cre lineage requires Ednrb for Ret Y1015 phosphorylation.
source: Thus, a substantial subpopulation of the Wnt1Cre lineage requires Ednrb for Ret Y1015 phosphorylation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the observations.

claim: Ednrb deficiency did not affect phosphorylation of Ret-Y1096 in Wnt1Cre-derived cells at E11.5.
source: Interestingly, Ednrb deficiency did not affect phosphorylation of Ret-Y1096 as demonstrated by positive staining in the Wnt1Cre+; Ret+ nuclei (Figure 7n and r).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with reference to Figure 7n and r.

claim: At least one feature of active Ret signaling in Wnt1Cre lineage cells requires the presence of Ednrb.
source: Although we (or other studies) have not yet proven the biological importance of Ret Y1015 in enteric progenitor migration, our results demonstrate that at least one feature of active Ret signaling in Wnt1Cre lineage cells requires the presence of Ednrb.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the observations.

claim: The ENS has a dual lineage origin as defined by the Pax2Cre and Wnt1Cre drivers.
source: Our study reveals that the ENS has a dual lineage origin as defined by the Pax2Cre and Wnt1Cre drivers.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the discussion.

claim: Cells of the Pax2Cre and Wnt1Cre lineages co-mingle in the pharyngeal region and co-migrate through the gut.
source: We observed that cells of the Pax2Cre and Wnt1Cre lineages co-mingle in the pharyngeal region and co-migrate through the gut.
evidence: This is stated as an observation in the discussion.

claim: Gut migration by each lineage is dependent on the other.
source: Indeed our observations indicate that gut migration by each lineage is dependent on the other.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the observations in the discussion.

claim: The Wnt1Cre lineage requires GDNF responsiveness to migrate past the stomach.
source: Thus, the Wnt1Cre lineage requires GDNF responsiveness to migrate past the stomach, whereas the Pax2Cre lineage migrated into the midgut and only became GDNF-dependent at the hindgut.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the discussion.

claim: The Pax2Cre lineage migrated into the midgut and only became GDNF-dependent at the hindgut.
source: Thus, the Wnt1Cre lineage requires GDNF responsiveness to migrate past the stomach, whereas the Pax2Cre lineage migrated into the midgut and only became GDNF-dependent at the hindgut.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the discussion.

claim: Edn3 signaling through Ednrb is required to support GDNF responsiveness and thereby to support cell migration in both the Pax2Cre and Wnt1Cre lineages.
source: Our studies demonstrate that Edn3 signaling through Ednrb is required to support GDNF responsiveness and thereby to support cell migration in both the Pax2Cre and Wnt1Cre lineages.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the discussion.

claim: Ret expression is induced or expanded by Ednrb signaling in Pax2Cre-derived cells.
source: We describe independent mechanisms to explain this relationship: Ret expression is induced or expanded by Ednrb signaling in Pax2Cre-derived cells, whereas in Wnt1Cre-derived cells, Ednrb induces competence for Ret signaling without changing Ret expression.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the discussion.

claim: In Wnt1Cre-derived cells, Ednrb induces competence for Ret signaling without changing Ret expression.
source: We describe independent mechanisms to explain this relationship: Ret expression is induced or expanded by Ednrb signaling in Pax2Cre-derived cells, whereas in Wnt1Cre-derived cells, Ednrb induces competence for Ret signaling without changing Ret expression.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the discussion.

claim: Phosphorylation of Ret Y1015 is known to activate the PLCg/PKC pathway.
source: Phosphorylation of this residue is known to activate the PLCg/PKC pathway (Mahato and Sidorova, 2020).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Mahato and Sidorova, 2020.

claim: Edn3-Ednrb signaling converges on GDNF-Ret function in both the Pax2Cre and Wnt1Cre lineages.
source: In any event, the conceptual conclusion that Edn3-Ednrb signaling converges on GDNF-Ret function in both the Pax2Cre and Wnt1Cre lineages is supported by both the in vitro and in vivo observations and helps to explain the common phenotype of Hirschsprung disease that is seen when any component is mutated.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the discussion.

claim: The severity of Hirschsprung disease with the same null mutation of Ednrb is highly dependent on strain background in rats and mice.
source: With the same null mutation of Ednrb, the severity of Hirschsprung disease is highly dependent on strain background in rats (Dang et al., 2011) and mice (Hosoda et al., 1994).
evidence: This is stated with citations to Dang et al., 2011 and Hosoda et al., 1994.

claim: In humans, Hirschsprung disease-associated mutations are almost always heterozygous (presumably haploinsufficient), but show variable extent of phenotypic penetrance.
source: Similarly, in humans, Hirschsprung disease-associated mutations are almost always heterozygous (presumably haploinsufficient), but show variable extent of phenotypic penetrance, even so far as to be inherited in some affected patients from one asymptomatic parent (Fuchs et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Fuchs et al., 2001.

claim: A human genome-wide association study demonstrated genetic interaction between the EDNRB and RET loci.
source: In some cases, the genetic background effect involves a mutation in a gene already known to be associated with Hirschsprung disease: a human genome-wide association study demonstrated genetic interaction between the EDNRB and RET loci (Carrasquillo et al., 2002), and synergy was evident in mice with intentional combinations of Ednrb and Ret (McCallion et al., 2003) or Ednrb and Sox10 (Cantrell et al., 2004) alleles.
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Carrasquillo et al., 2002.

claim: Synergy was evident in mice with intentional combinations of Ednrb and Ret alleles.
source: In some cases, the genetic background effect involves a mutation in a gene already known to be associated with Hirschsprung disease: a human genome-wide association study demonstrated genetic interaction between the EDNRB and RET loci (Carrasquillo et al., 2002), and synergy was evident in mice with intentional combinations of Ednrb and Ret (McCallion et al., 2003) or Ednrb and Sox10 (Cantrell et al., 2004) alleles.
evidence: This is stated with a citation to McCallion et al., 2003.

claim: Synergy was evident in mice with intentional combinations of Ednrb and Sox10 alleles.
source: In some cases, the genetic background effect involves a mutation in a gene already known to be associated with Hirschsprung disease: a human genome-wide association study demonstrated genetic interaction between the EDNRB and RET loci (Carrasquillo et al., 2002), and synergy was evident in mice with intentional combinations of Ednrb and Ret (McCallion et al., 2003) or Ednrb and Sox10 (Cantrell et al., 2004) alleles.
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Cantrell et al., 2004.

claim: Mice on an ICR background with conditional or global Ednrb deficiency die consistently around 3 weeks of age.
source: In this light, it was striking that mice on an ICR background with conditional or global Ednrb deficiency die consistently around 3 weeks of age.
evidence: This is stated as an observation in the discussion.

claim: In congenital sensorineural deafness, the penetrance of hearing impairment in ICR background Edn3 or Ednrb mutant mice is variable (approx. 50%).
source: Interestingly, in congenital sensorineural deafness, the other major EDN3-EDNRB phenotype that with Hirschsprung disease defines Waardenburg-Shah syndrome type IV, the penetrance of hearing impairment in ICR background Edn3 or Ednrb mutant mice is variable (approx. 50%) (Tan et al., 2023).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Tan et al., 2023.

claim: Different modifiers interact with Edn3-Ednrb in auditory development vs. ENS development.
source: This indicates that different modifiers interact with Edn3-Ednrb in auditory development vs. ENS development.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the observation in the discussion.
